description: This topic explains the meaning and importance of agriculture, the physical and human factors that influence it, the main farming systems and crops in Tanzania and Africa, the problems facing agriculture and their solutions, and how it compares with farming in developed countries.

mcq.questionText: What is the meaning of agriculture?

options.text: The mining of minerals from the ground
The growing of crops and the keeping of livestock
The building of houses and roads
The catching of fish from the sea

mcq.explanation: Agriculture is the practice of cultivating crops and rearing animals (livestock) for food, raw materials and income.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a PHYSICAL factor influencing agriculture?

options.text: Availability of capital
Government policy
Climate
Market demand

mcq.explanation: Climate (rainfall, temperature, sunlight) is a physical factor. Capital, policy and market are human factors.

mcq.questionText: A farmer who grows food mainly to feed his own family is practising which type of agriculture?

options.text: Commercial agriculture
Plantation agriculture
Subsistence agriculture
Market gardening

mcq.explanation: Subsistence agriculture is farming for home consumption, with little or no surplus for sale.

mcq.questionText: Which crop is grown on large plantations in the Tanga region of Tanzania and used to make ropes and bags?

options.text: Tea
Sisal
Coffee
Maize

mcq.explanation: Sisal is a major plantation crop in Tanga and Morogoro. Its strong fibres are used to make ropes, sacks and mats.

mcq.questionText: Shifting cultivation involves which of the following practices?

options.text: Clearing land, farming it until it loses fertility, then moving to a new area
Growing one crop on the same land every year
Keeping animals on a fenced ranch
Watering crops using canals all year round

mcq.explanation: In shifting cultivation a farmer clears and uses a plot, then abandons it for a new plot once the soil is exhausted.

mcq.questionText: Which farming system involves moving with herds of cattle in search of water and pasture?

options.text: Ranching
Mixed farming
Nomadic pastoralism
Irrigation farming

mcq.explanation: Nomadic pastoralism is the keeping of livestock while moving from place to place looking for pasture and water, as practised by the Maasai.

mcq.questionText: Which region of Tanzania is most famous for growing coffee on the slopes of Mount Kilimanjaro?

options.text: Mtwara
Kilimanjaro
Dodoma
Lindi

mcq.explanation: The cool, fertile volcanic slopes of Mount Kilimanjaro are well known for arabica coffee growing.

options.text: Growing crops and keeping livestock on the same farm
Growing only cash crops for export
Mixing different chemicals in the soil
Keeping many different wild animals

mcq.explanation: Mixed farming combines crop cultivation and livestock keeping on the same farm, so the two activities support each other.

mcq.questionText: Why is irrigation farming important in dry areas of Tanzania such as parts of Dodoma?

options.text: It removes the need for any soil
It supplies water to crops where rainfall is low or unreliable
It stops all pests from attacking crops
It makes crops grow without sunlight

mcq.explanation: Irrigation provides water artificially through canals, sprinklers or pumps, allowing farming where rainfall is insufficient.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a major problem facing agriculture in Tanzania?

options.text: Too much modern machinery
Over-reliance on unreliable rainfall
Too many good roads to the market
Excessive use of fertilisers everywhere

mcq.explanation: Most farming depends on rain (rain-fed agriculture), so unreliable rainfall and droughts often cause crop failure.

mcq.questionText: Market gardening (horticulture) is BEST described as the growing of:

options.text: Cereals on very large plantations far from towns
Vegetables, fruits and flowers for sale, often near towns
Timber trees in natural forests
Grass for feeding cattle on ranches

mcq.explanation: Market gardening is the intensive growing of vegetables, fruits and flowers for sale, usually located close to urban markets.

mcq.questionText: Cashew nuts in Tanzania are mainly grown in which part of the country?

options.text: The southern coast (Mtwara and Lindi)
The northern highlands
The Lake Victoria shores
The central plateau of Dodoma

mcq.explanation: Cashew nuts are an important export crop grown mainly in the southern coastal regions of Mtwara and Lindi.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following describes ranching?

options.text: Moving cattle daily over long distances
Keeping large herds of livestock on a fenced, permanent area of land
Growing rice in flooded fields
Growing vegetables in small plots

mcq.explanation: Ranching is commercial livestock keeping on large fenced areas where animals graze in one settled place, such as NARCO ranches.

mcq.questionText: How does agriculture contribute to Tanzania's economy?

options.text: It provides employment, food and export earnings
It only provides minerals for export
It reduces the number of jobs available
It has no effect on national income

mcq.explanation: Agriculture employs most Tanzanians, supplies food, provides raw materials for industry and earns foreign exchange through exports.

mcq.questionText: Wheat farming in countries like Canada and the USA differs from most farming in Tanzania because it is mainly:

options.text: Small-scale and done by hand
Large-scale and highly mechanised
Done only for home consumption
Practised without any capital

mcq.explanation: Wheat farming in developed countries is large-scale, commercial and uses machines such as combine harvesters, while Tanzanian farming is mostly small-scale.

fib.questionText: The growing of crops and the keeping of animals for food and income is called _____.
fib.explanation: Agriculture covers both crop cultivation and livestock keeping.

fib.questionText: Farming done mainly to feed the farmer's own family is known as _____ agriculture.
fib.explanation: Subsistence agriculture produces mainly for home use rather than for sale.

fib.questionText: Farming carried out on a large scale mainly to sell the produce for profit is called _____ agriculture.
fib.explanation: Commercial agriculture is large-scale production aimed at selling for profit.

fib.questionText: The supplying of water to crops artificially through canals or pipes is called _____.
fib.explanation: Irrigation provides water to crops where natural rainfall is not enough.

fib.questionText: The plantation crop grown around Tanga and used to make ropes and sacks is _____.
fib.explanation: Sisal fibre from Tanga and Morogoro is used to make ropes, bags and mats.

fib.questionText: A farming system in which crops are grown and livestock are kept on the same farm is called _____ farming.
fib.explanation: Mixed farming combines crop and livestock production on one farm.

fib.questionText: The keeping of livestock while moving from place to place in search of pasture and water is called _____ pastoralism.
fib.explanation: Nomadic pastoralism, as practised by the Maasai, involves constant movement of herds.

fib.questionText: The intensive growing of vegetables, fruits and flowers for sale near towns is called market gardening or _____.
fib.explanation: Horticulture (market gardening) is the growing of vegetables, fruits and flowers for the market.

fib.questionText: The cash crop grown mainly on the southern coast of Tanzania in Mtwara and Lindi is the _____ nut.
fib.explanation: Cashew nuts are a key export crop of the southern coastal regions.

fib.questionText: Commercial livestock keeping on a large, fenced and permanent piece of land is called _____.
fib.explanation: Ranching keeps large herds on fenced land in a settled area, unlike nomadic herding.

tf.questionText: Agriculture includes both the growing of crops and the keeping of livestock.
tf.explanation: Agriculture covers crop cultivation and animal rearing.

tf.questionText: Climate, soil and relief are examples of human factors influencing agriculture.
tf.explanation: Climate, soil and relief are physical (natural) factors, not human factors.

tf.questionText: Subsistence farming is mainly carried out to produce crops for sale and large profits.
tf.explanation: Subsistence farming is mainly for home consumption, not for large-scale sale.

tf.questionText: Coffee is an important cash crop grown on the slopes of Mount Kilimanjaro.
tf.explanation: The cool fertile slopes of Kilimanjaro are well known for coffee production.

tf.questionText: In shifting cultivation, the farmer stays on the same plot of land permanently.
tf.explanation: In shifting cultivation the farmer moves to a new plot once the soil loses fertility.

tf.questionText: Ranching involves keeping livestock on a large fenced area in a settled place.
tf.explanation: Ranching is settled, commercial livestock keeping on fenced land.

tf.questionText: Irrigation is useful only in areas that receive very heavy rainfall throughout the year.
tf.explanation: Irrigation is most useful in dry areas where rainfall is low or unreliable.

tf.questionText: Unreliable rainfall and droughts are among the major problems facing agriculture in Tanzania.
tf.explanation: Most Tanzanian farming depends on rain, so drought and unreliable rainfall cause crop failure.

tf.questionText: Wheat farming in developed countries such as Canada is mainly small-scale and done by hand.
tf.explanation: Wheat farming in developed countries is large-scale and highly mechanised using machines like combine harvesters.

tf.questionText: Agriculture provides raw materials for industries such as cotton for textile factories.
tf.explanation: Crops like cotton and sisal supply raw materials to industries, linking agriculture to manufacturing.

summary.correctAnswer: Agriculture is the growing of crops and the keeping of livestock for food, raw materials and income.
summary.explanation: It combines crop cultivation and animal rearing.

summary.questionText: Give two physical factors that influence agriculture.
summary.correctAnswer: Climate and soil (also relief and water).
summary.explanation: Physical factors are natural conditions such as climate, soil, relief and water supply.

summary.questionText: Give two human factors that influence agriculture.
summary.correctAnswer: Capital and labour (also market, technology and government policy).
summary.explanation: Human factors are those created or controlled by people, such as money, workers, markets and policy.

summary.questionText: Differentiate between subsistence and commercial agriculture.
summary.correctAnswer: Subsistence agriculture produces mainly for the family's own use, while commercial agriculture produces on a large scale for sale and profit.
summary.explanation: The main difference is the purpose: home consumption versus selling for profit.

summary.questionText: Explain what is meant by shifting cultivation.
summary.correctAnswer: Shifting cultivation is a system where a farmer clears and uses a plot of land, then moves to a new plot when the soil loses fertility.
summary.explanation: Land is abandoned to recover its fertility while the farmer opens new land.

summary.questionText: Name three major cash crops grown in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Coffee, cotton and sisal (also tea, cashew nuts and tobacco).
summary.explanation: These are important export and industrial crops in Tanzania.

summary.questionText: Distinguish between nomadic pastoralism and ranching.
summary.correctAnswer: Nomadic pastoralism involves moving livestock from place to place for pasture and water, while ranching keeps livestock on a large fenced area in a settled place.
summary.explanation: Nomadism is mobile and traditional; ranching is settled and commercial.

summary.questionText: State three problems facing agriculture in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Unreliable rainfall/drought, poor markets and prices, and use of poor or traditional farming tools (also pests, diseases and shortage of capital).
summary.explanation: These problems reduce production and the incomes of farmers.

summary.questionText: Suggest three solutions to the problems facing agriculture in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Use irrigation to reduce dependence on rain, improve markets and prices, and use modern tools, fertilisers and improved seeds (also farmer education and credit).
summary.explanation: Solutions aim at increasing and stabilising production and farmer incomes.

summary.questionText: State three ways in which agriculture is important to the economy of Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: It provides employment, supplies food, earns foreign exchange through exports and provides raw materials for industries.
summary.explanation: Agriculture is the backbone of the economy, supporting jobs, food security, trade and industry.

hoq.questionText: A district in central Tanzania receives low and unreliable rainfall, yet the government wants to increase food crop production there. Which combination of measures would be MOST effective and sustainable?

options.text: Encourage shifting cultivation over a wider area each year
Develop irrigation schemes and promote drought-resistant crops such as sorghum and millet
Move all farmers into nomadic pastoralism
Ban all farming until the rains become reliable

hoq.explanation: In dry, unreliable-rainfall areas, irrigation supplies water artificially and drought-resistant crops survive low rainfall, so together they raise and stabilise production sustainably.

hoq.questionText: Two farmers grow maize on similar soil. Farmer A uses a hand hoe, local seeds and no fertiliser; Farmer B uses a tractor, improved seeds and fertiliser. Which statement BEST explains the likely difference in their output?

options.text: Farmer A will produce more because hand hoes protect the soil better
Both will produce the same because soil is the only factor that matters
Farmer B will produce more because better technology, inputs and capital raise yields per area
Farmer B will produce less because machines always damage crops

hoq.explanation: Human factors like capital, technology and improved inputs increase efficiency and yields, so Farmer B with modern methods is likely to produce far more from the same land.

hoq.questionText: Compare large-scale wheat farming in Canada with maize farming by a typical smallholder in Tanzania. Which set of differences is CORRECT?

options.text: Canadian wheat farming is small-scale and manual, while Tanzanian maize farming is fully mechanised
Both are large-scale, mechanised and produce only for export
Canadian wheat farming is large-scale, mechanised and commercial, while Tanzanian smallholder maize farming is small-scale, labour-intensive and often for subsistence
Both use no capital and depend only on family labour

hoq.explanation: Wheat farming in developed countries uses large farms, machinery and high capital for commercial output, whereas typical Tanzanian smallholders farm small plots using mostly manual labour, often for home use.
